summary.prose: This Epic gives VS Code users a read-only delivery board: one place to see every epic, story, task and issue, the stage each has reached and why, and the separate approval, review and validation evidence behind it. A reader can find work that needs a decision, follow an epic down to a task and the record that supports it, and see contradictory or incomplete evidence plainly instead of having it hidden behind a single status label. The board changes nothing; it only reads what the workflow has already recorded.

body.problem: Developers, reviewers and delivery leads who work in VS Code still cannot see delivery as a whole. The daemon now assembles every epic, story, task and issue, with its stage, its evidence and its approval, review and validation signals, into one coherent view, but nothing in the editor shows it. To learn what is ready, what needs a decision or why an item looks finished, a reader must still open and cross-read individual documents one at a time, and the facts that matter most are the ones that are easiest to miss that way: a build that was approved although some of its task checks failed, a review that blocks an unapproved design, a defect whose parent cannot be found, or a record that could not be read at all. Because the view is reachable only as raw data, its distinctions between workflow progress, human approval, automated review and task validation are lost on the way to the reader, and the only document surface in the editor shows one pending document at a time, so it cannot answer questions that span many items or show completed and in-progress work side by side.

nonGoals.text: Creating, approving, rejecting or editing any work item or record from the board, or moving work between stages.
nonGoals.rationale: The first release is read-only by the PRD's scope (FR-09); controlled actions need their own interaction and workflow design.

nonGoals.text: Deriving stages, routes, identities, attention or conflicts in the editor.
nonGoals.rationale: The daemon owns interpretation (PRD §07); a second derivation in the client would drift from the first and from the JetBrains board that follows.

nonGoals.text: Changing the existing VS Code document review pane.
nonGoals.rationale: That pane belongs to Epic bfe98ff7; the board opens evidence in it but does not alter it.
Deferred to E3, a parity pass after this Epic settles the interaction decisions.

nonGoals.text: Automatic refresh, live agent activity, review annotations or agent handoff.
nonGoals.rationale: The daemon sends nothing unsolicited, live activity cannot be inferred from records, and annotations are an unframed follow-on (PRD §02, §10).

nonGoals.text: Assignees, sprints, due dates, priorities, estimates or external tracker synchronisation.
nonGoals.rationale: Out of scope for the first release per PRD §02.

assumptions.text: The delivery view published by E1 (workflow.delivery and workflow.deliveryEvidence, schemaVersion 1) is the board's only data source, and later changes to it are additive optional fields.
A dedicated editor tab is the right primary placement, to be checked against a sidebar entry in the first story.
Manual refresh is enough for the first release.

The delivery view does not carry a task's dependencies or acceptance checks, only its validation result, so showing them needs either the plan record read through the daemon or an additive field in the delivery view; which one is a design decision for the HLD.

"Complete" stays as the final stage's label; whether readers take it for validation success is tested in a usability session that the epics plan assigns to S2, outside this Define's acceptance criteria.

constraints.text: The board reads delivery data only through the daemon's IPC; it never opens the daemon's databases or reads the artifact store's files itself.
The board displays the stage, route, attention and conflict facts the daemon publishes and does not derive or override them.
No navigation, filter, expansion or refresh changes any artifact, approval, source file or Git state.

Artifact text is rendered as data: embedded HTML or scripts are never executed, and file navigation goes only through the host's existing authorised viewer, never to arbitrary paths taken from artifact content.
Only one coherent snapshot is applied at a time; a superseded response is dropped and never merged with a newer one.
A failed refresh keeps the last successful view with a stale or error notice, and an empty workspace, an unavailable daemon and a failed read are distinct states.
After data arrives, the initial board renders within one second for a 1,000-artifact, 500-item fixture, and each local filter change responds within 150 ms.
The board's webview follows the plugin's existing pattern of a restrictive Content-Security-Policy on every webview document.
The same snapshot and filters always produce the same order and counts.

The existing review pane (Epic bfe98ff7) gains one additive entry point that opens a given artifact by id, read-only when it is not pending; its list, rendering and approval behaviour are otherwise unchanged, and the board opens evidence through that entry point.

Every colour-coded state also has a text label, every control and evidence entry is reachable by keyboard with visible focus, card selection and refresh results are announced without excessive chatter, and a narrow pane keeps every item and warning reachable.

stories.title: Open the board, refresh it, and see why it is empty, unavailable or incomplete
stories.userValue: A reader can open the delivery board in an editor tab, refresh it when they choose, and always know whether what they see is current, stale, empty or only partly readable, so they never mistake missing data for missing work.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a workspace whose daemon is running
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the delivery board
acceptanceCriteria.then: the board opens in an editor tab showing the work items of one snapshot and the time that snapshot was taken

acceptanceCriteria.given: the board is showing a snapshot
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user refreshes and the refresh fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the last successful board stays visible with a notice that names the failure and the time of the last successful refresh

acceptanceCriteria.given: a workspace with no recorded work, a daemon that cannot be reached, a read that fails, and a snapshot that reports unreadable records
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board is opened in each case
acceptanceCriteria.then: each case shows its own distinct state and message, and the partly readable case still shows every readable item

acceptanceCriteria.given: two refreshes are requested in quick succession
acceptanceCriteria.when: the response to the earlier request arrives after the later one
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the later snapshot is shown and nothing from the earlier snapshot is mixed into it

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user has a filter applied and an item selected
acceptanceCriteria.when: a refresh succeeds and the item still exists
acceptanceCriteria.then: the filter and the selection are kept; if the item no longer exists the selection is cleared and the user is told

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository under version control with recorded workflow artifacts
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the board and refreshes it repeatedly
acceptanceCriteria.then: no artifact, approval, source file or Git state changes

localConstraints.text: The editor-tab placement is checked against a sidebar entry point before this Story completes, and the decision is recorded.

functionalRequirements.statement: The user can open the delivery board from a command and refresh it on demand.
functionalRequirements.rationale: FR-07; refresh is manual in the first release.

functionalRequirements.statement: The board shows when its current data was taken and, after a failed refresh, the failure and the time of the last success.
functionalRequirements.rationale: FR-07 and the PRD's freshness rule.

functionalRequirements.statement: The board distinguishes an empty workspace, an unavailable daemon, a failed read and partially readable data.

stories.title: See every work item in its stage column, with its signals, and narrow the board
stories.userValue: A reader can scan the whole delivery picture by stage, see at a glance which items carry an approval, review, validation or conflict signal, and narrow the board to one epic, to standalone work, to a search or to what needs attention, with every count agreeing with what they see.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a snapshot with stories and issues at every stage
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: it shows six columns in workflow order, Scoped, Design & plan, Ready · design approved, Ready · plan approved, Build recorded and Complete, and each story or issue appears exactly once, in the column the snapshot assigns it

acceptanceCriteria.given: a story whose build record is approved but holds failed task results
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: its card sits in Complete and carries a validation-conflict badge with a text label

acceptanceCriteria.given: an unapproved design whose review blocks it
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user turns on the Needs attention filter
acceptanceCriteria.then: the card shows a review-blocked badge, matches the filter, and stays in its own stage column

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user selects one epic and enters a search
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board updates
acceptanceCriteria.then: the cards, column counts and totals all agree with each other, including cards hidden behind a show-more control, and clearing the search and the scope restores the previous set

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same snapshot loaded twice with the same filters, including items with equal timestamps
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board renders each time
acceptanceCriteria.then: the order of cards and every count are identical

acceptanceCriteria.given: a work item title or notice that contains markup or script text
acceptanceCriteria.when: its card renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: the text is shown literally and nothing in it runs

functionalRequirements.statement: Each card shows the item's title, kind, whether it is standalone, and text-labelled badges for approval, review, validation, conflict and data-quality notices.
functionalRequirements.rationale: FR-02; colour is never the only signal.

functionalRequirements.statement: The user can search, scope to one epic or to standalone work, and filter to items that need attention, using the daemon's attention decision.
Every displayed count reflects the current selection, including items not yet shown on screen.

stories.title: See progress per epic and follow defects to the work that fixes them
stories.userValue: A delivery lead can see how far each epic has progressed with counts that say what they count, keep standalone work separate from epic work, and follow each defect to its fix stories, including defects whose parent cannot be found.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an epic with five stories of which two are complete
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the epic rollup
acceptanceCriteria.then: the epic shows a completion count that names its denominator, such as 2 of 5 stories complete, and its stories grouped by stage

acceptanceCriteria.given: standalone stories and standalone issues alongside epics
acceptanceCriteria.when: the epic rollup renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: standalone work is shown in its own group and is not counted towards any epic

acceptanceCriteria.given: an issue that links to a story, and another issue whose parent cannot be resolved
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the issue view
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first shows a relationship the user can follow to the story, and the second is still listed with an unresolved-parent notice

acceptanceCriteria.given: an issue with more than one fix story
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the issue view
acceptanceCriteria.then: the issue shows each fix story as a distinct child with its own stage

acceptanceCriteria.given: a search or epic scope applied on the board
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user switches to the epic rollup or the issue view
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same selection applies and the counts agree with the board

functionalRequirements.statement: The epic rollup shows each epic's progress with counts that name what they count, and keeps standalone work separate.
The issue view lists every issue with its fix stories and its parent relationship, or a notice when the parent cannot be resolved.

stories.title: Open a work item to see its tasks, why it is in its stage, and the records behind it
stories.userValue: A developer or reviewer can open any item and see its tasks with their dependencies, checks and recorded results, the reason for its stage, and every supporting record with its approval and review, then open each record to read it, so they can explain an item's state without searching the records by hand.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a story whose plan lists tasks and whose build record has results for some of them
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the story's details
acceptanceCriteria.then: each planned task shows its dependencies and acceptance checks and is labelled Passed, Failed or Unrecorded, a task present only in the build record is labelled unplanned, and Unrecorded tasks are not counted as passed or failed

acceptanceCriteria.given: any work item
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens its details
acceptanceCriteria.then: the details show the daemon's stated reason for the item's stage and the records that reason cites

acceptanceCriteria.given: a story whose build is approved although some task results failed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens its details
acceptanceCriteria.then: the approval and the failed results are shown together with an explanation of the conflict, and neither is hidden

acceptanceCriteria.given: a rejected record, a record with a review override, and an approved record with a historical blocking review
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user reads their evidence entries
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rejection is labelled rejected, not pending, and the original review verdict is shown together with any override

acceptanceCriteria.given: an evidence record the existing document viewer can open, and a build record that viewer cannot open
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens each
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first opens in the existing review pane and the second is shown read-only from the daemon, with its text rendered as data

acceptanceCriteria.given: a story that has a code review but no build record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens its details
acceptanceCriteria.then: its stage is unchanged, a review-without-build notice (the PRD's unledgered code review) explains the situation, and the code review is listed in its evidence

localConstraints.text: Whether a record opens in the existing review pane or is read through the daemon follows the open-with value the daemon publishes for that record.

functionalRequirements.statement: Item details show nested tasks with dependencies, acceptance checks and recorded results, linked issues and full source identity.
Item details explain the stage and let the user open each supporting record.

stories.title: Use the board in a narrow pane, with the keyboard alone, and at either density
stories.userValue: Every reader, including keyboard-only and screen-reader users and those working in a narrow pane, can reach the same work, warnings and evidence, and a large workspace stays responsive.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the board open in a narrow pane
acceptanceCriteria.when: it renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: columns become a grouped list by stage and every card, badge and warning remains available

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user who uses only the keyboard
acceptanceCriteria.when: they move through the views, open an item's details and close them again
acceptanceCriteria.then: every control and evidence entry is reachable with visible focus, and closing the details returns focus to where they were

acceptanceCriteria.given: a screen reader
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user moves between cards and refreshes
acceptanceCriteria.then: every colour-coded state has a text label, and card selection and the refresh result are announced once

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user switches between compact and comfortable density
acceptanceCriteria.when: the board re-renders
acceptanceCriteria.then: no warning, badge or accessibility label is hidden at either density

acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture of 1,000 records forming 500 work items on the reference environment
acceptanceCriteria.when: the snapshot arrives and the user then changes a filter
acceptanceCriteria.then: the initial board renders within one second and each filter change responds within 150 ms

functionalRequirements.statement: The board adapts to a narrow pane by grouping items by stage without dropping information.
The board is fully operable by keyboard and screen reader.
functionalRequirements.rationale: AC-14 and the PRD's accessibility rule.

functionalRequirements.statement: The user can choose compact or comfortable card density.
The board meets the agreed render and filter response targets for a large workspace.

requirements.statement: The board shows every work item in the delivery view in exactly one stage column, with its approval, review, validation and conflict signals shown as separate facts.
requirements.rationale: The PRD's product principle: a convenient status label must not conceal contradictory evidence.

requirements.statement: The board offers a board view, an epic rollup view and an issue view over the same delivery view, and every count shown agrees with the cards the current selection contains.
A reader can search, scope to one epic or to standalone work, and filter to items that need attention, and clearing a filter restores the previous set.

A reader can open any work item's details, see its tasks and the reason for its stage, and open each supporting record in the editor's existing document viewer, or read it through the daemon when that viewer cannot open it.
requirements.rationale: FR-05 and FR-06; the existing viewer reads a record by artifact id through workflow.artifactContent, which finds the record from the insrc:artifact marker in its markdown, and on 2026-10-08 only 24 of the 93 build-record markdown files carried that marker.

requirements.rationale: FR-07, FR-08 and the PRD's freshness rule.

citations.quotedText: Product principle: preserve the difference between workflow progress, human approval, automated review, and task validation. A convenient status label must not conceal contradictory evidence.
E2 opens evidence *in* that pane but does not change it, so it should be framed as **new**, with `bfe98ff7` as an adjacent boundary.
Fix sc7 in this HLD, version it with schemaVersion, and allow only additive optional fields after approval; any breaking change goes through an HLD amendment before E2 consumes it.
readonly tasks:            readonly TaskValidation[];
The production IDE client obtains a normalized read model through daemon IPC; it does not open the daemon’s databases or independently interpret artifact files.
FR-09Keep the MVP read-only: all navigation and filtering leave artifacts, approvals, code, and Git state unchanged.
Safe rendering: render artifact text as data. Never execute embedded HTML/scripts or follow arbitrary file paths from artifact content. File navigation must use the host’s existing authorized viewer.
Concurrency: apply one coherent snapshot at a time. Drop superseded responses; do not combine half of an old snapshot with half of a newer one.
Placement: a dedicated editor tab is the leading candidate for a wide board; validate against a tool-window entry point.
Refresh strategy: manual refresh is sufficient for the first increment; confirm whether existing daemon events can support later automatic updates.
| Completion wording | Keep "Complete"; test it in E2's usability session | E2 S2 |
